2607.08443.title: ADORN: Adaptive Drift handling for Open RAN using Reinforcement Learning
2607.08443.paper_summary: Dynamic traffic variations in Open Radio Access Networks (O-RAN) lead to drift, which degrades the performance of Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) models. Traditional retraining approaches maintain forecasting accuracy but incur high computational cost and may lead to violations of Service Level Agreements (SLAs). This work proposes a Q-learning-based adaptive retraining approach that formulates the retraining decision as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), where a Reinforcement Learning (RL) agent learns a policy that balances forecasting accuracy and retraining cost. The proposed approach incorporates a multi-expert Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) ensemble to mitigate catastrophic forgetting and improve robustness across diverse traffic conditions. Experimental results show that the proposed approach effectively reduces retraining overhead compared to greedy and random baselines, while maintaining system performance within predefined limits.
2607.08443.paper_summary_zh: 動態交通變化在開放無線接入網絡（O-RAN）中導致漂移，這會降低人工智能/機器學習（AI/ML）模型的性能。傳統的再訓練方法雖然能維持預測準確性，但會產生高計算成本，並可能導致違反服務水平協議（SLA）。本研究提出了一種基於Q學習的自適應再訓練方法，將再訓練決策公式化為馬爾可夫決策過程（MDP），其中增強學習（RL）代理學習一種平衡預測準確性和再訓練成本的策略。所提出的方法結合了多專家長短期記憶（LSTM）集成，以減輕災難性遺忘並改善在多樣化交通條件下的穩健性。實驗結果顯示，與貪婪和隨機基準相比，所提出的方法有效減少了再訓練開銷，同時保持系統性能在預定範圍內。
